meta.title: Houston-region local government, 16 days of posts
meta.subject: local government in the Houston region — Harris County Commissioners Court and Judge Lina Hidalgo, Houston City Council and Mayor John Whitmire, Montgomery County Commissioners Court, county and city budgets, bonds, development regulations, and the fights among them
meta.subtitle: Oct 1 to Oct 16, 2026. Each dot is one post with 1K+ views about Houston-region local government, plus every post repeating an earlier one, in the lane for what it argues. Higher and bigger means more views. White means 90% or more the same words as an earlier post, with a white line back to it. Coloured lines link a post to the post it quoted or replied to. Updated daily.

lanes.label: Democrats raised Harris County taxes
lanes.description: Democratic control of Commissioners Court has driven up homeowner tax bills and the tax rate, and officials like Briones are accused of wasting taxpayer money (billboards, Pride events) while claiming budgets are tight.

lanes.label: Race to replace Hidalgo
lanes.description: The Plummer vs. Sanchez contest for county judge is a referendum on Democratic control of the county, with Plummer attacked as absent and anti-police and Hidalgo's falling approval used as a talking point.

lanes.label: Whitmire's budget gap and controller fights
lanes.description: Mayor Whitmire's administration is portrayed as chaotic and overreaching: a growing city budget shortfall, clashes with the controller over contracts and adviser pay, and a federal grant filed without council approval.

lanes.label: Hidalgo as Democratic cautionary tale
lanes.description: Hidalgo's 2023 treatment stay is used as a smear and as a supposed pattern of Democrats hiding unstable candidates, notably in the rumor about Talarico and the Ohio facility.

lanes.label: Surveillance, policing and ICE fights
lanes.description: Local officials are fought over public safety and surveillance: Flock camera data and oversight, the ICE implications of a federal grant, and whether Democrats are soft on police.

lanes.label: Infrastructure, growth and flood spending
lanes.description: Posts argue over whether governments are spending on the right priorities: drainage, roads, transit, data centers, housing, homelessness, and the stadium, against tight budgets.

lanes.label: Pushback
lanes.description: Posts doubting, mocking, fact-checking or arguing against the dominant framings.

posts.name: Spencer Pratt
posts.text:
Guys. Let me share a little "secret" about campaigns...there's calculus behind EVERYTHING. And I do mean everything. Every word. Every image. Every debate quip. Everything, down to the color of the font you choose, is calculated to invoke a specific feeling, and most of the time, it's easy to decipher what the campaign is trying to convey with these choices, and that is the goal. 

So if you find yourself confused by something happening in a campaign, and you're thinking "why would they do that?"...like..."how the hell could they think going radio silent for 2 weeks is a good idea in the closing weeks of a campaign?" They don't think it's a good idea. It's because the alternative is so much worse. If you think going radio silent and getting TORCHED online for over a week in the closing month of a $400M campaign is bad...just imagine how bad the real story was.

You don't get to choose everything that happens in the campaign, but you do THINK about everything that happens in a campaign and choose your strategy for presenting it to the public or spinning it. Sometimes...there is no good way of spinning it, so you just have to eat your shit sandwich, and hope that the alternative would've been worse.  

It's a lot like the current LA Mayor's race...there is no good option.

His campaign continues to say he was home recovering from a severe case of the flu, but brand new flight logs tell a different story. 

A private Cessna Citation X (N750MF, operated by Jet Linx Aviation) departed the Austin area on October 8, overnighted at Butler County Regional Airport (HAO) in Hamilton, Ohio, and returned to Austin, landing at approximately 10:24 a.m. on October 9, just hours before Talarico was seen at ACL that afternoon.

Hamilton airport is a small regional field roughly 20 minutes from the Lindner Center of HOPE in Mason, Ohio, a private inpatient mental health and behavioral health facility.

Talarico's connection to that facility is that a good friend of his, Harris County Judge Lina Hidalgo, checked into this mental hospital for a multi-week mental health leave in 2023.

"What are the chances that a private plane took off from Austin and flew to tiny Hamilton airport in Ohio which is 20 mins from the Lindner Center, a private inpatient mental health treatment facility, and then turned around and flew back to Austin landing yesterday morning at 10:24am right before James Talarico magically reappears at the Austin City Limits music festival that afternoon? Lindner Center also happens to be the same facility that Talarico’s good friend and Harris County Judge Lina Hidalgo spent 7 weeks in when she had a mental breakdown 3 years ago…

So many coincidences!"

The Talarico campaign has refused to answer whether or not he was at Lindner or any other facility. The campaign has dismissed the mental-health speculation that circulated earlier and maintains the absence was due to the flu.

However, the new flight logs throw several questions into this timeline. Talarico's opponent Ken Paxton is still demanding answers.

This story is still developing. Stay tuned for more updates....

James Talarico is lying again.
A private jet based in Austin, Texas, flew to a small airport about 20 minutes from a well-known private inpatient mental health center in Ohio, then returned to Austin the next morning (yesterday) landing hours before James Talarico reappeared in public after almost two weeks of being 'missing' that his campaign blamed on the flu. 
#austin
Public flight tracking confirms the aircraft’s flight between Austin and Butler County Regional Airport (HAO) in Hamilton, Ohio.
Rumors started circulating that Talarico's absence was due to a mental health breakdown, according to numerous sources, and his campaign flew out to retrieve him when the online chatter became too big to contain.  
Details: 

➡The plane is N750MF, a Cessna Citation X operated by Jet Linx Aviation and based in the Austin area.  

➡TFlight data shows it left Austin for Hamilton, Ohio, on October 8 and returned the following morning, landing in Austin around 10:23 a.m. local time.  

➡THamilton’s airport is a short drive from the Lindner Center of HOPE in Mason, Ohio - which is a private, nonprofit facility offering inpatient, residential, and outpatient psychiatric care for adults and adolescents. 

➡This is the same center that Harris County Judge Lina Hidalgo checked herself into in 2023 and spent seven weeks at for mental health treatment. It cost about $88,000. 

Talarico, who's running against Attorney General Ken Paxton for U.S. Senate, had not held an in-person campaign event in Texas since around September 26.  

On September 30 he joined a Hispanic Business Council event virtually and said he had gone to urgent care in Dallas the night before:  

Then he went 'missing.' 

Campaign spokesman JT Ennis repeated the flu excuse and said Talarico would return to the trail over the weekend. He didn't.  

On October 9, after the plane landed, Talarico appeared at the Austin City Limits Music Festival.  

Ennis posted video and wrote that Talarico was “still alive and meeting with voters at ACL today.” 

But people aren't buying the flu excuse saying the schedule doesn't match the timeline, and the flight from Austin to Ohio is too much of a coincidence.  

Timeline:  

🔵Monday, September 28, 7 p.m., downtown Manhattan fundraiser:  
➡️Tickets ran from $500 to $27,000. Talarico attended.  

🔵Tuesday, September 29, Greenwich Village, a second fundraiser, on his campaign’s invitation.   
➡️Tickets ran from $1,000 to $13,500. He held the reception.   

🔵A Tuesday night reception in Greenwich Village, New York and a Tuesday night urgent-care visit in Dallas is not the same thing.   
The campaign hasn't given an explanation, proof of a flight, a timestamp, or even a clinic name.   

While Talarico was in New York collecting out of state money - his events in Texas were being cancelled.   

➡️The Edinburg forum on September 30 went virtual.  
➡️The Central Texas African American Civic Engagement Symposium was canceled.   
➡️An Austin fundraiser set for Tuesday was scrapped.  

Paxton’s campaign launched a tip line and circulated missing-person-style posters.  

At a San Antonio rally with President Trump, Paxton led the crowd in asking “Where is James Talarico?”  

President Trump called him “MISSING IN ACTION” on Truth Social and wrote that “12 days is a long time to rid yourself of the so-called flu bug.”  

Paxton’s team said Talarico “appears to be having a full-blown mental Tala-freak-out” and demanded proof of life.  

Los Angeles former Mayoral candidate Spencer Pratt said Talarico was in a mental health facility and that the campaign had stopped actively planning events, according to his sources.  

No hospital records, staff statements, or campaign acknowledgment has confirmed an urgent care visit in Dallas.  

What do you think happened? Did Talarico really have the flu for 2 weeks? Or did he have a mental health breakdown? 

Pratt says whatever Talarico was 'out with' is way worse than claiming to have the flu for 13 days!!!
